payload: Toyota Motor Co. founded as spinoff from Toyoda Automatic Loom Works.
'Just-in-time' (JIT) concept introduced as flow-production principle inspired by Ford's River Rouge + supermarket replenishment.
Eiji Toyoda + colleagues visit Ford River Rouge plant; decision to adapt rather than copy Ford methods.
Ohno assigned to apply JIT in machine shop; first kanban-card pull-system experiments; codified as Toyota Production System (TPS).
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 2 p. 21-22; Spear & Bowen 1999 HBR p. 96-97

payload: Andon-cord rule codified: any operator can stop the line on detecting abnormality; line-stop is a learning event not a failure.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 11 p. 129-138; Spear & Bowen 1999 p. 99

payload: SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) developed; die-change time reduced from hours to minutes; enables small-batch production.
Standard-work format codified: takt time + work sequence + standard work-in-process per workstation; documents revised by operators not engineers.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 12 p. 142-150; Spear & Bowen 1999 p. 98

payload: 5 Whys root-cause practice codified: any FAILURE event triggers iterated 'why?' interrogation to find root cause not symptom.
Kaizen (continuous improvement) institutionalized: every employee expected to submit improvement suggestions; suggestion volume tracked annually.
Oil crisis exposes Detroit overproduction; Toyota's small-batch JIT becomes competitive advantage; substrate visible internationally.
A3 problem-solving format codified: single 11x17 sheet structure (background, current state, target, analysis, countermeasures, plan, follow-up); mentor-mentee review cycle.
Ohno publishes 'Toyota Production System' (Japanese edition); TPS substrate partially exposed in print.
NUMMI plant (Fremont CA): worst-performing GM plant reopens under Toyota management; quality + productivity rise to Toyota-Japan levels with same workforce.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 2 p. 23-26; Adler 1993 (cited in Liker)

payload: Keiretsu supplier-development: long-term tier-1 supplier relationships; Toyota engineers embedded at supplier facilities to teach TPS at supplier substrate level.
Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky (TMMK) starts production; first US wholly-owned Toyota plant; staffed by US workers trained by Japanese senshu (mentors).
'The Machine That Changed the World' published; first wide Western-language exposition of lean production based on MIT International Motor Vehicle Program 5-year study.
TSSC (US-based nonprofit) formed: Toyota teaches TPS to non-automotive Western organizations (Bose, hospital systems, etc.); explicit substrate-not-snapshot transfer model.
'Toyota Way' internal document drafted; codifies operating principles for global rollout.
source_citation: Liker 2004 introduction + ch. 1; Toyota 2001 internal document referenced

payload: Annual kaizen suggestion counts: Toyota averages 1M+ suggestions/year company-wide; ~99% implementation rate (aggregated; Maximum-granularity rule §2.3 applied).
Spear & Bowen publish 'Decoding the DNA of the Toyota Production System' in HBR; four rules codified as observer-side reading of Toyota substrate.

Spear's 'four rules' (as reported): (1) all work highly specified as to content/sequence/timing/outcome; (2) every customer-supplier connection direct; (3) pathway for every product simple and direct; (4) improvements made using scientific method at lowest possible level under teacher guidance.
Senshu (master-mentor) lineage formalized: each new TPS implementation overseas matched with Japanese senshu for 3-5 years; mentorship traceable to Ohno disciples.
Periodic line-stop events (andon cord pulls) treated as continuous learning data; per Toyota internal: ~1000+ andon pulls per plant per day at mature plants.
Unintended-acceleration recall crisis: 9M+ vehicles recalled; $1B+ in settlements; CEO Akio Toyoda testifies before US Congress; major public FAILURE event triggers post-mortem.
source_citation: NHTSA records 2009-2010; Toyota 20-F FY2010-FY2011 SEC filings; Liker & Convis 2011 (post-recall analysis)

payload: Post-recall internal audit explicitly diagnoses cause as overshoot of growth + thinning of senshu lineage at new plants; remediation = restoration of mentor density per TPS substrate principles.
source_citation: Liker & Convis 2011 (cited in TPS literature); Toyota 2011 sustainability report

payload: Toyota Way 2020 update internal document; reinforces TPS substrate after 2009-10 recall.
Western manufacturers (GM, Ford, Boeing, US healthcare systems, etc.) initiate 'Lean transformation' programs based on Spear & Bowen 1999 + Womack-Jones-Roos 1990 + Liker 2004 published descriptions.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 22 p. 285-287 (catalog of imitator programs); Spear 2009 ch. 8 (failures)

payload: Imitators install andon cords, kanban cards, takt-time boards, A3 templates as visible artifacts.
Empirically: andon cord present but workers culturally inhibited from pulling; quota-driven culture penalizes line stops.
source_citation: Spear & Bowen 1999 p. 100-103 (Aluminum Co. case); Liker 2004 ch. 22 p. 285

payload: Standard work documents written by industrial engineers not operators; documents become compliance instruments not living substrate; revision frequency near zero.
5 Whys not paired with on-the-floor scientific-method culture; root-cause investigations stop at first plausible blame.
Kaizen suggestion programs launched with quarterly volume targets; suggestion volume rises briefly then collapses; ~95% of programs abandoned within 3 years.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 22 p. 290-292 (Toyota TSSC observation of imitator programs)

payload: Supplier-relationships managed under traditional adversarial-bid contracting; no embedded-engineer model; supplier-development logs not created.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 17 p. 218-220 (Big Three vs Toyota supplier contrast)

payload: Senshu / master-mentor lineage not imported: lean consultants brought in for 6-12 month engagements; no multi-year mentor matching; mentor lineage absent.
NUMMI dissolution 2010: even GM (with 25 years inside NUMMI) failed to propagate the substrate to other GM plants; NUMMI closed during GM bankruptcy.
source_citation: Liker 2004 ch. 2 retrospective; press coverage 2010 NUMMI closure

payload: 'Lean Six Sigma' certification industry produces ~1M+ certified practitioners; near-zero documented sustained substrate transformation; certifications are snapshots of Spear's four rules without log generation.
